calls.head: The Sabres’ edge in shot quality
calls.body: The Sabres are around the middle of the league for shot quality, and the Wild are near the bottom. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one.
calls.call: The Sabres’ shots are more dangerous on average than the Wild’s.

calls.head: Where the Wild have the edge: shots from in close
calls.body: The Wild are one of the league’s best for shots from in close, and the Sabres are around the middle. That’s the biggest gap between these two, and it isn’t a big one. Shots from in close tend to be the more dangerous ones.

surprises.head: Buffalo hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: Buffalo’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 47, against their usual 95 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 20 games.

story.head: Östlund sparks the Sabres back from two down
paras: Danila Yurov got the scoring started for the Wild on the power play midway through the second. Maxim Shabanov scored his first goal for Minnesota less than two minutes later to make it 2-0. Noah Östlund pulled the Sabres within one early in the third, and Tage Thompson tied it 2-2 midway through the period. Owen Power won it in overtime.

The Sabres carried the play, outshooting the Wild 28-20, but needed overtime to win it. The Wild hit a post and the crossbar and still lost. Colten Ellis made 18 saves for the Sabres, and Jesper Wallstedt kept the Wild in it, stopping 25 of 28. The Sabres moved to 2-1-0 and climbed to fourth in the Atlantic, while the Wild dropped to 2-0-1, slipping out of first in the NHL.
